jobs.title: Head of Finance
jobs.description:
$150,000–$180,000 a year

Tuition reimbursement, Paid time off, Vision care, Dental care, Life insurance, Employee assistance program, Disability insurance, Discounted or free food

Permanent, Full-time

Hybrid work in 4445 Lougheed Highway W, Burnaby, BC

About Us:

Entertainment Partners is a global organization that has been a trusted production partner to the entertainment industry for over 45 years, helping clients create and produce great shows, choose the best production location, forecast, manage and track expenses, and pay crew and talent. As a global leader in entertainment payroll, production finance and production management solutions, EP delivers integrated, digital solutions to support every phase of production. EP brings together background casting and digital production technology with the Casting Portal, the leading SaaS-based platform that has transformed the way background actors are found, hired, managed and paid, and the iconic and legendary Central Casting.
Entertainment Partners Canada is the lead provider of financial services to the entertainment industry in Canada. We provide financial services to the Motion Picture, Television and Commercial industries along with production management and accounting software services. Entertainment Partners Canada prides itself on being the best in class from a product/services perspective but we are equally proud to have been Great Places to Work certified since 2017, providing an encouraging, accepting, and interesting work experience for all of our valued employees.
Job Summary:

The candidate is EP Canada's senior finance leader — strategic partner to the Canadian leadership team and primary Canadian counterpart to EP's global finance and FP&A organizations. The role delivers Canadian financial planning, analysis, and reporting capability into a global FP&A framework, and is accountable for controllership, statutory reporting, cash management, and the integrity of all Canadian accounting systems, controls, and financial information.
Working closely with the President, Canada and department leaders across Sales, Client Services, Payroll, Incentives, Operations, HR, and Technology, the candidate turns operating information into forecasts, business cases, and business narrative that shape investment, pricing, and resourcing decisions. In parallel, the role partners daily with the global FP&A team on planning, forecasting, and management reporting, and with the broader finance organization — CFO, Corporate Controller, Tax, and Treasury — to ensure Canadian results are reported accurately, forecasts are aligned to global planning cadences, and cross-border obligations are met.
The candidate adheres to the accounting policies and procedures approved by the CFO, company leadership, and Board of Directors and ensures the integrity of all accounting systems and financial information. The Candidate's duties are performed consistently with the company's mission and values, and must adhere to company policies and procedures.
Key Duties and Responsibilities:

Strategic partnership with Canadian leadership:

Serve as strategic finance partner/advisor to the President, Canada and the Canadian leadership team, providing financial analysis, recommendations, and decision support on investment, pricing, resourcing, and other business-critical decisions.
Partner with Canadian department leaders across Sales, Client Services, Payroll, Incentives, Operations, HR, and Technology; translate operating information into financial insight and support business cases, ROI analyses, and pricing and margin reviews for new and existing service lines.
Serve on the EP Canada Senior Management team and other policy-making committees, representing the financial and commercial implications of business decisions.

Canadian controllership and Partnership with Global Finance:

Acts as the senior Canadian finance leader, ensuring local results are accurately represented within EP's global reporting following all statutory rules and standards.
Serves as the key liaison with US Tax, external auditors, and regulatory bodies (CRA, provincial ministries) on cross-border and compliance matters. (examples: T106, T1134, Part XIII withholding, and ULC-specific treatment)
Responsible for annual audit
Owns the full close-to-reporting cycle for Canada, from general ledger through statutory financial statements, under both Canadian and US GAAP frameworks.
Maintains the control environment — internal controls, segregation of duties, and account reconciliations — underpinning the integrity of Canadian financial reporting.
Partners with Finance Operations to ensure payment and transactional processes are timely, accurate, and well-controlled.
Brings a continuous improvement lens to the close process, starting with a 90-day current state assessment and roadmap.

Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A) — Canadian delivery:

Serve as the Canadian finance lead, partnering with global FP&A team and working within the planning framework, calendar, and templates; personally deliver the Canadian components of the annual operating plan, quarterly reforecast, monthly variance analysis, multi-year planning, and scenario modelling.
Own Canadian financial data quality and the Canadian forecasting rhythm across revenue, margin, headcount, capital expenditure, and cash; identify risks and opportunities against plan and surface them to Canadian leadership and global FP&A.
Partner with the global FP&A team on management reporting, KPIs, and dashboards; ensure the Canadian view is accurate, current, and appropriately contextualized in consolidated reporting.
Prepare and present financial updates for board packages, quarterly business reviews, annual operating plans, quarterly forecasts, and town halls.

Treasury, cash, and risk management:

Oversee the local cash management function including maintaining Canadian banking relationships; monitor corporate cash flows, fraud detection, vendor credit risk profiles, and forecast restricted/unrestricted cash balances, and recommend foreign exchange and hedging actions in coordination with Global Treasury.
Manage insurance coverage for the organization in coordination with US Risk Management, including compliance obligations.

Team leadership and continuous improvement:

Lead, develop, and evaluate the Canadian finance team, including recruitment, training, and succession planning; make recommendations on salary increases and annual bonus amounts.
Lead change and continuous improvement initiatives across finance systems, processes, and reporting to support the business's evolving needs, including ERP and reporting system enhancements.
Set and implement short-term and long-term departmental goals, objectives, policies, and operating procedures.
Perform other related duties as needed.

Qualifications:

Essential:

Ten years+ progressive experience in a senior-level finance or accounting position
CPA designation required
Experience operating in the Canadian entity of a US-parented multinational, including US GAAP consolidation and cross-border reporting into a US head office.
Demonstrated experience partnering with executive or senior leadership on business-critical decisions, translating financial analysis into commercial and operational recommendations.
Strong hands-on operational finance capability — management reporting and analysis, scenario modelling — with the ability to personally deliver the work, not only supervise others doing it; experience operating as the local FP&A partner within a global/head-office-led FP&A framework is strongly preferred.
Strong financial storytelling and executive presentation skills — able to translate results and forecasts into clear business narrative that lands with both a Canadian President and the global executive team.
Track record of out-of-the-box thinking when challenged with process improvement, re-organization, major system rehaul
Working knowledge of Canadian tax (T2, GST/HST/PST), statutory reporting, and audit; familiarity with transfer pricing and cross-border tax obligations.
Strong ERP and reporting systems experience.
Executive-level communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to influence stakeholders outside of Finance (written and verbal).
Ability to lead teams to produce quality output within tight timeframes and manage multiple concurrent priorities.
Commercial or operational business acumen beyond core accounting and finance, with comfort operating in a matrix organization.

Preferred:

Familiarity with the film and television production ecosystem or experience adjacent to production companies, studios, or service providers.
Experience with Oracle ERP
Private equity-owned or PE-backed environment experience.
Comfort operating across the three-hour Toronto/Vancouver time difference and asynchronously with a US head office.

Why Work with EP:

Group RRSP
Extended health and dental benefits
Hybrid work environment
Casual dress code
Employee snack program
Health and Wellness Spending Account
Movie ticket reimbursement
Employee Assistance Program

Working conditions

Conditions are normal for an office environment

This position offers an expected compensation of $150,000–$180,000 per year, depending on skills and experience. This range reflects the anticipated salary for the successful candidate and complies with Ontario’s pay transparency requirements.

The tool reviews resumes against the qualifications and requirements in this posting and ranks applications based on job-related criteria. Commitment to Supporting Accessibility Needs

EP Canada welcomes and encourages applications from people with disabilities. Accommodations are available on request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process. As only short-listed candidates will be contacted, we thank you in advance for your interest in EP!

Director, Finance Operations
jobs.description:
Competition # :
50401

Opportunities and Social Development

Location:
HALIFAX

Type of Employment:
Permanent

Union Status:
Exclusion - Non Union - NSPG

Closing Date:
19-Nov-26 (Applications are accepted until 11:59 PM Atlantic Time)

About Us

At the Department of Opportunities and Social Development (OSD), we are a large and diverse department providing a broad portfolio of programs and services including Child and Family Wellbeing (CFW), Income Assistance (IA), Supportive Housing and Homelessness, and the Disability Support Program (DSP).

Through our services, we advocate and help vulnerable Nova Scotians be independent, self-reliant, and secure. We work collaboratively across the province with a strong, dedicated network of supports and staff to achieve desired and shared outcomes for all.

About Our Opportunity

Financial leadership in OSD has a direct connection to the programs, services and external providers that support Nova Scotians. As Director of Finance, you will lead a complex, province-wide financial operation and help ensure that leaders have the accurate information, practical advice and effective controls needed to make responsible decisions.

This is an opportunity to combine professional accounting expertise with broader leadership. You will guide financial operations, strengthen planning and risk management, support sound decision-making, and lead a sizeable team through competing priorities and organizational change. Your success will depend not only on technical knowledge, but also on your judgement, communication, relationship-building, and ability to help others deliver results.

Primary Accountabilities

In this role, you have the opportunity to lead a substantial finance function, advise senior decision-makers and improve the systems and practices that support programs and services across Nova Scotia. A few of your key responsibilities are to:

Provide strategic and operational financial advice to the Executive Director and senior leaders, translating complex financial and non-financial information into clear options, risks and recommendations.
Lead the delivery and continuous improvement of financial operations that support departmental programs, regional teams and external service providers.
Provide leadership for budgeting, forecasting, financial analysis and the management of cost pressures, helping leaders make informed choices about resources and program delivery.
Strengthen financial accountability through effective internal controls, risk management, transparent reporting and compliance with applicable accounting standards and government financial policies.
Lead, support and develop a geographically distributed finance team. Set clear direction, build management capability, encourage collaboration and create the conditions for people to take ownership of their work.
Provide clear direction and leadership to managers and staff by establishing priorities, clarifying accountabilities, delegating effectively and supporting consistent delivery across the finance function.
Build the capability and resilience of the finance team through workforce planning, coaching, performance management and succession development.
Exercise sound professional judgment and critical thinking in interpreting and applying provincial government financial policies and applicable accounting standards within complex and diverse contexts, considering both financial and non-financial information.
Build productive relationships across OSD and with central agencies, internal audit, legal partners, service providers and other stakeholders. Address difficult issues with diplomacy while maintaining professional standards and public accountability.
Lead practical improvements to financial processes, systems and service delivery. Sequence change thoughtfully so that essential operations remain stable and responsive.
Represent the department on relevant cross-government initiatives, committees and working groups, and communicate financial issues clearly to both financial and non-financial audiences.

Qualifications And Experience

You are a designated Chartered Professional Accountant (CPA) with progressively responsible experience leading financial operations and people in a complex organization. Your experience demonstrates that you can:

lead managers and professional staff in a complex work environment, including setting expectations, delegating responsibility, developing capability and addressing performance concerns.
assess workforce and organizational needs, strengthen team capacity and guide employees through operational or organizational change while maintaining service delivery.
prepare and deliver briefings or presentations for executive-level audiences, including providing credible financial advice and explaining complex issues
support budgeting, forecasting, financial analysis and the management of significant or competing financial pressures;
establish or strengthen internal controls, accountability and risk-management practices;
build effective relationships and resolve difficult issues with sound judgement, discretion and diplomacy; and
organize work, adapt to changing priorities and deliver accurate advice within tight timeframes.

You bring a practical understanding of professional accounting standards and the ability to apply financial policy in a complex operating environment. You also understand that strong financial management requires attention to program and service outcomes, not only financial results.

The Following Experience Would Be Considered An Asset

audit, assurance or control-review work;
public-sector, human-services, not-for-profit or other complex service-delivery finance;
financial relationships with funded organizations, service providers, grants or contribution agreements;
Public Sector Accounting Standards and government financial policy

We will assess the above qualifications and competencies using one or more of the following tools: written examination, standardized tests, oral presentations, interview(s), and reference checks.

Equivalency

We recognize equivalent combinations of training, education, and experience, providing opportunities for individuals with diverse backgrounds to contribute their skills and expertise. Applicants relying on education and experience equivalencies must demonstrate such equivalencies in their application.

Benefits

Based on the employment status, the Government of Nova Scotia offers its employees a wide range of benefits such as a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, Health, Dental, Life Insurance, General illness, Short- and Long-Term Disability, Vacation and Employee and Family Assistance Programs. For information on all our Benefit program offerings, click here: Benefits for government employees.

Working Conditions

Your typical work week is 35 hours with 7-hour days. The role includes regular travel to regional offices and other work sites across Nova Scotia.

Additional Information

An offer of employment is conditional upon satisfactory completion of all applicable background checks and confirmation of credentials, including: Education Verification and Criminal Background Check.

What We Offer

Career Development where you have access to career guidance, tools, resources, and ongoing training for every stage of your career
Engaging workplace: our Employees feel valued, respected, connected, and tuned in, we have forward-thinking policies and strategies
Countless career paths

jobs.title: Director, Equipment Planning and Biomedical Services
jobs.description:
Job Description

The Director, Equipment Planning and Biomedical Services is accountable for clinical and non-clinical asset planning, maintenance and management. The role provides overall leadership to Mackenzie Health equipment needs for short-term and long-term asset planning, tracking, maintenance, management, and refresh. The director is responsible for overseeing all facility and redevelopment work required to plan, procure, and complete installation of medical equipment. This role also provides Director-level leadership to the Central Equipment and Biomedical Engineering departments. This role works within an environment that has Design-Build-Finance-Maintain (DBFP) equipment relationships, Managed Equipment Services (MES) contract, as well as a traditional in-house biomedical engineering service and support model. This role also works closely with Mackenzie Health Redevelopment department to plan, procure, and implement the Furniture, Fixtures, and Equipment (FF&E) components of various redevelopment projects. Additionally, the Director coordinates efforts with various departments to develop and maintain a multi-year equipment plan and budget, ensuring appropriate inventory levels, mitigation of corporate risk, and balances demand with broader organizational need.

Primary Responsibilities

Maintain current knowledge of laws, ordinances, and regulations pertaining to corporate purchasing practices.
Working in close collaboration with corporate procurement, develop a multi year clinical technology strategy, in conjunction with clinical and nonclinical leaders, and that aligns with organizational priorities. The strategy must include centralized purchasing/procurement of materials, equipment, machinery, and services required for operations, projects, and capital investments.
Responsible for the implementation of all Equipment projects from needs identification through to commissioning and on-going maintenance.
Manage and oversee all aspects of large-scale equipment installation projects including managing internal and external stakeholders, shop drawing reviews, scope of work development, project schedule development, budget management, reporting, commissioning, training, and close-out documentation.
Work collaboratively with the Digital Health portfolio to ensure all required integrations are planned and implemented to support equipment use.
Provide executive leadership with strategic and tactical advice, as well as risks and opportunities related to emerging healthcare technologies and long-term organizational planning.
Provide advice to management at all levels by using knowledge of equipment market and procurement.
Working in close collaboration with corporate procurement, supervise or manage complex negotiations to settle commercial disputes and claims with suppliers by establishing goals and approving commercial settlements.
Manage the Philips MESP contract ($300M+ over 14-year contract life) and provide support to Philips and the Mackenzie Clinical team in the administration of the MESP contracted services.
Provide direct leadership to Biomedical Engineering and Central Equipment staff and services across a multi site hospital system.
Establish policies and procedures supporting safe equipment use and maintenance.
Lead service contract procurement and negotiations.
Monitor vendor performance and service level agreements.
Develop performance KPI for adequate service and support of medical equipment.
Work with multiple equipment vendors to coordinate design and construction activities, monitor performance and intervene to rectify issues.
Ensure the development and maintenance of work systems, goals and objectives, management systems, teamwork, and resource management for departments within the area of accountability.
Create and maintain asset management and tracking workflows and processes.
Create and maintain a space management program.
Space management includes oversight and recommendations to resolve all space requests. Working collaboratively with Redevelopment, Facilities, Clinical, Clinical Support Teams to ensure space allocations are prioritized and allocated based on hospital priorities.
Act as Chair of the Change Request Group (SAFES) to ensure alignment with corporate vision and mission.
Manage the intake, review, and implementation of all changes related to Space, Aesthetics, Furniture, Equipment, and Signage.
Provide leadership, support, and direction to program staff on issues related to performance, corporate direction, service delivery, staff development, Human Resources Management (HRM), realignment, and change management strategies.
Direct the process of establishing, implementing, and reporting on appropriate quality and productivity indicator measurement tools, based on provincial benchmarks, best practice standards, and legislative requirements.
Co-develop annual budgets and operating plans that align with the hospital’s programs and directives, and ensure the program stays within budget.
Ensure all assigned employees comply with hospital, government, and customer policies, procedures, and regulations.
Build external and internal business relationships to gather information, identify market and industry trends, build partnership and alliances to support and facilitate the hospital’s objectives and plans.
Management of Regulatory Requirements as applicable to equipment installations ensuring all documentation is submitted and approved by appropriate regulatory bodies to support the installation and use of medical equipment (e.g. HARP, CNSC).
Ensure effective procurement activities that meet the requirements and needs of the hospital’s internal stakeholders.
Ensure a safe environment for patients, staff, and visitors; investigate, report, debrief and take or direct corrective action as appropriate on incidents.
Manage human resources which include recruitment, selection and training.
Teach, coach and lead staff in the development and monitoring of quality indicators and improvement initiatives.
Collaborate with internal and external stakeholders/organizations/community groups to achieve program objectives, integrate, and link services and foster partnerships across the continuum of service delivery.
Participate in education and training specific to current, relevant federal and provincial health and safety legislation, standards, and guidelines.

What must you have?

Minimum of a Master’s Degree or Master’s ready in Business, Economics, or in a related field, from an accredited university.
Minimum of 5-10 years experience working in equipment planning and procurement within a health care environment.
Minimum of five (5) years’ working in a senior leadership role, preferably in a health care environment.
Biomedical service leadership experience is required or similar experience that is deemed equivalent.
Training or recent experience with drafting requests for proposals and vendor agreements is required.

What else do you bring?

Strong knowledge of hospital operations.
Demonstrated experience in negotiating and managing large, complex contracts.
Demonstrated knowledge of the appropriate tools for grading, analyzing, and assessing materials, equipment, supplies, services, and other commodities.
Demonstrated knowledge of Supply Chain Management (SCM), Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP), and Material Requirements Planning (MRP) software.
Demonstrated excellent critical and logical thinking, analysis, and reasoning to identify underlying principles, reasons, or facts.
Demonstrated project management, change management, and analytical thinking skills.
Demonstrated ability to lead, motivate, and influence individuals and teams toward a vision, while maintaining group cohesiveness and effectiveness.
Demonstrated strategic business sense with financial management and budget development skills.
Demonstrated understanding of interrelationships between clinical and support programs.
Demonstrated ability to manage complex systems and human resources at the executive level.
Demonstrated leadership skills with ability to foster relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
Demonstrated ability to coach, advise and teach others using the principles of adult learning.
Demonstrated training, experience, or utilization of lean methodology for process improvement.
Demonstrated ability to independently identify issues, plan improvements, measure success and continue improvement.
Proven attendance record.
Demonstrates understanding and complies with patient and staff safety policies and procedures that foster a safe and inclusive environment for all.
Ability to perform the essential duties of the job.
Effectively uses empathy in interactions with others.
Demonstrates behaviours consistent with Mackenzie Health’s Commitment to Caring.
Models behaviour that is aligned with the values of Mackenzie Health – Excellence, Leadership and Empathy.
Commitment to providing an exceptional experience for staff and clients within a challenging and exciting health care environment.

Preferably, Your Profile Also Includes

Additional specialized training will be considered an asset (e.g. Professional Certification in Supply Chain Logistics (P. Log) or a Designation as a Supply Chain Management Professional (SCMP).
You may be required to work at any site of Mackenzie Health.

Mackenzie Health is an inclusive and equal opportunity employer committed to providing accommodations for applicants upon request at any stage of the recruitment process in accordance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA) and the Ontario Human Rights Code.

Our hiring process does not involve the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to screen, assess or select applicants.

We thank all applicants for their interest; however, only those under consideration for an interview will be contacted.

jobs.title: Vice President – AI Infrastructure
jobs.description:
Vice President – AI Infrastructure | Toronto

Pearse Partners is working with a leading global investment platform to hire a Vice President to join its AI Infrastructure team in Toronto.

This is an exciting opportunity to join a growing investment team focused on one of the most rapidly developing areas of the infrastructure market, with exposure to investments supporting the expansion of AI and next-generation technology.

The Opportunity:

Lead the evaluation, execution and management of AI infrastructure investments.
Gain exposure to opportunities across data centres, digital infrastructure and AI-related infrastructure.
Take ownership of complex M&A transactions, financial modelling and due diligence processes.
Work closely with senior leadership on investment strategy and portfolio development.
Play a key role in supporting the growth of the platform and developing junior team members.

The Ideal Candidate:

Investment banking or private equity experience, ideally at the VP level.
Strong financial modelling, valuation and transaction execution capabilities.
Exposure to M&A, infrastructure, TMT or technology-related investments.
Genuine interest in AI, digital infrastructure and emerging technologies.
Strong leadership, commercial judgement and communication skills.

Location: Toronto, Canada
Open to candidates based in the US
Position: Vice President – AI Infrastructure

For further information or a confidential discussion, please feel free to reach out directly.

new_jobs.title: Director, Equipment Planning and Biomedical Services
new_jobs.description:
Job Description

The Director, Equipment Planning and Biomedical Services is accountable for clinical and non-clinical asset planning, maintenance and management. The role provides overall leadership to Mackenzie Health equipment needs for short-term and long-term asset planning, tracking, maintenance, management, and refresh. The director is responsible for overseeing all facility and redevelopment work required to plan, procure, and complete installation of medical equipment. This role also provides Director-level leadership to the Central Equipment and Biomedical Engineering departments. This role works within an environment that has Design-Build-Finance-Maintain (DBFP) equipment relationships, Managed Equipment Services (MES) contract, as well as a traditional in-house biomedical engineering service and support model. This role also works closely with Mackenzie Health Redevelopment department to plan, procure, and implement the Furniture, Fixtures, and Equipment (FF&E) components of various redevelopment projects. Additionally, the Director coordinates efforts with various departments to develop and maintain a multi-year equipment plan and budget, ensuring appropriate inventory levels, mitigation of corporate risk, and balances demand with broader organizational need.

Primary Responsibilities

Maintain current knowledge of laws, ordinances, and regulations pertaining to corporate purchasing practices.
Working in close collaboration with corporate procurement, develop a multi year clinical technology strategy, in conjunction with clinical and nonclinical leaders, and that aligns with organizational priorities. The strategy must include centralized purchasing/procurement of materials, equipment, machinery, and services required for operations, projects, and capital investments.
Responsible for the implementation of all Equipment projects from needs identification through to commissioning and on-going maintenance.
Manage and oversee all aspects of large-scale equipment installation projects including managing internal and external stakeholders, shop drawing reviews, scope of work development, project schedule development, budget management, reporting, commissioning, training, and close-out documentation.
Work collaboratively with the Digital Health portfolio to ensure all required integrations are planned and implemented to support equipment use.
Provide executive leadership with strategic and tactical advice, as well as risks and opportunities related to emerging healthcare technologies and long-term organizational planning.
Provide advice to management at all levels by using knowledge of equipment market and procurement.
Working in close collaboration with corporate procurement, supervise or manage complex negotiations to settle commercial disputes and claims with suppliers by establishing goals and approving commercial settlements.
Manage the Philips MESP contract ($300M+ over 14-year contract life) and provide support to Philips and the Mackenzie Clinical team in the administration of the MESP contracted services.
Provide direct leadership to Biomedical Engineering and Central Equipment staff and services across a multi site hospital system.
Establish policies and procedures supporting safe equipment use and maintenance.
Lead service contract procurement and negotiations.
Monitor vendor performance and service level agreements.
Develop performance KPI for adequate service and support of medical equipment.
Work with multiple equipment vendors to coordinate design and construction activities, monitor performance and intervene to rectify issues.
Ensure the development and maintenance of work systems, goals and objectives, management systems, teamwork, and resource management for departments within the area of accountability.
Create and maintain asset management and tracking workflows and processes.
Create and maintain a space management program.
Space management includes oversight and recommendations to resolve all space requests. Working collaboratively with Redevelopment, Facilities, Clinical, Clinical Support Teams to ensure space allocations are prioritized and allocated based on hospital priorities.
Act as Chair of the Change Request Group (SAFES) to ensure alignment with corporate vision and mission.
Manage the intake, review, and implementation of all changes related to Space, Aesthetics, Furniture, Equipment, and Signage.
Provide leadership, support, and direction to program staff on issues related to performance, corporate direction, service delivery, staff development, Human Resources Management (HRM), realignment, and change management strategies.
Direct the process of establishing, implementing, and reporting on appropriate quality and productivity indicator measurement tools, based on provincial benchmarks, best practice standards, and legislative requirements.
Co-develop annual budgets and operating plans that align with the hospital’s programs and directives, and ensure the program stays within budget.
Ensure all assigned employees comply with hospital, government, and customer policies, procedures, and regulations.
Build external and internal business relationships to gather information, identify market and industry trends, build partnership and alliances to support and facilitate the hospital’s objectives and plans.
Management of Regulatory Requirements as applicable to equipment installations ensuring all documentation is submitted and approved by appropriate regulatory bodies to support the installation and use of medical equipment (e.g. HARP, CNSC).
Ensure effective procurement activities that meet the requirements and needs of the hospital’s internal stakeholders.
Ensure a safe environment for patients, staff, and visitors; investigate, report, debrief and take or direct corrective action as appropriate on incidents.
Manage human resources which include recruitment, selection and training.
Teach, coach and lead staff in the development and monitoring of quality indicators and improvement initiatives.
Collaborate with internal and external stakeholders/organizations/community groups to achieve program objectives, integrate, and link services and foster partnerships across the continuum of service delivery.
Participate in education and training specific to current, relevant federal and provincial health and safety legislation, standards, and guidelines.

What must you have?

Minimum of a Master’s Degree or Master’s ready in Business, Economics, or in a related field, from an accredited university.
Minimum of 5-10 years experience working in equipment planning and procurement within a health care environment.
Minimum of five (5) years’ working in a senior leadership role, preferably in a health care environment.
Biomedical service leadership experience is required or similar experience that is deemed equivalent.
Training or recent experience with drafting requests for proposals and vendor agreements is required.

What else do you bring?

Strong knowledge of hospital operations.
Demonstrated experience in negotiating and managing large, complex contracts.
Demonstrated knowledge of the appropriate tools for grading, analyzing, and assessing materials, equipment, supplies, services, and other commodities.
Demonstrated knowledge of Supply Chain Management (SCM), Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP), and Material Requirements Planning (MRP) software.
Demonstrated excellent critical and logical thinking, analysis, and reasoning to identify underlying principles, reasons, or facts.
Demonstrated project management, change management, and analytical thinking skills.
Demonstrated ability to lead, motivate, and influence individuals and teams toward a vision, while maintaining group cohesiveness and effectiveness.
Demonstrated strategic business sense with financial management and budget development skills.
Demonstrated understanding of interrelationships between clinical and support programs.
Demonstrated ability to manage complex systems and human resources at the executive level.
Demonstrated leadership skills with ability to foster relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
Demonstrated ability to coach, advise and teach others using the principles of adult learning.
Demonstrated training, experience, or utilization of lean methodology for process improvement.
Demonstrated ability to independently identify issues, plan improvements, measure success and continue improvement.
Proven attendance record.
Demonstrates understanding and complies with patient and staff safety policies and procedures that foster a safe and inclusive environment for all.
Ability to perform the essential duties of the job.
Effectively uses empathy in interactions with others.
Demonstrates behaviours consistent with Mackenzie Health’s Commitment to Caring.
Models behaviour that is aligned with the values of Mackenzie Health – Excellence, Leadership and Empathy.
Commitment to providing an exceptional experience for staff and clients within a challenging and exciting health care environment.

Preferably, Your Profile Also Includes

Additional specialized training will be considered an asset (e.g. Professional Certification in Supply Chain Logistics (P. Log) or a Designation as a Supply Chain Management Professional (SCMP).
You may be required to work at any site of Mackenzie Health.

Pearse Partners is working with a leading global investment platform to hire a Vice President to join its AI Infrastructure team in Toronto.

This is an exciting opportunity to join a growing investment team focused on one of the most rapidly developing areas of the infrastructure market, with exposure to investments supporting the expansion of AI and next-generation technology.

The Opportunity:

Lead the evaluation, execution and management of AI infrastructure investments.
Gain exposure to opportunities across data centres, digital infrastructure and AI-related infrastructure.
Take ownership of complex M&A transactions, financial modelling and due diligence processes.
Work closely with senior leadership on investment strategy and portfolio development.
Play a key role in supporting the growth of the platform and developing junior team members.

The Ideal Candidate:

Investment banking or private equity experience, ideally at the VP level.
Strong financial modelling, valuation and transaction execution capabilities.
Exposure to M&A, infrastructure, TMT or technology-related investments.
Genuine interest in AI, digital infrastructure and emerging technologies.
Strong leadership, commercial judgement and communication skills.

Location: Toronto, Canada
Open to candidates based in the US
Position: Vice President – AI Infrastructure
